newsitem.title: PAPUA NEW GUINEA: New PNG PM Skate appoints 28-strong ministry.
newsitem.headline: New PNG PM Skate appoints 28-strong ministry.

text.p: Papua New Guinea Prime Minister Bill Skate on Tuesday appointed a 28-strong ministry, with Chris Haiveta as deputy prime minister, Roy Yaki as finance minister and Castan Maibawa petroleum and energy minister.
The ministry, which included 10 ministers from the former government of ousted prime minister Sir Julius Chan, was sworn in by the South Pacific nation's governor general.
Skate did not give himself a portfolio.
Haiveta, who was criticised by a judicial inquiry into a US$36 million mercenary deal, retained his deputy prime ministership, but lost the finance portfolio in favour of planning.
Yaki, leader of the People's Democratic Movement and previously in opposition, was appointed finance minister.
Former police minister Maibawa gained Petroleum and Energy, while Kilroy Genia retained the job of foreign minister.
True to his earlier pledge, Skate appointed a Bougainvillean, Sam Akoipai, as the minister in charge of the secessionist-wracked Bougainville island.
Akoipai was the leader of the government-backed resistence on the island.

Skate was elected prime minister last week after a surprise last minute decision to join the former ruling coalition to form a new government. Skate's decision was in stark contrasted to his strident election campaign against the former government, which he accused of corruption.
A voter backlash against political corruption saw more than 50 politicians, including 15 ministers, lose their seats at the June election.
